messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: slicing with indices to expand?
parts:
In R, if I have the vectors

    a = c('a','b','c') #some short vector
    b = c(2,3,3,2,1,1,1,2,3,2,2) #some longer vector of indicies

I can use the longer vector to slice the shorter vector into a longer vector:

    print(a[b])
    # "b" "c" "c" "b" "a" "a" "a" "b" "c" "b" "b"

Can this be done in some manner with stan? When I try to do as above, I get the parser error "expression denoting integer required; found type=int[1]"

If this were possible, it would really help me vectorize my code.

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

No, we don't have this. It's on our to-do list, so we'll
get there eventually.

It's actually slower in a compiled language like Stan to
build up vectors of indices vs. defining in a loop.

- Bob
